title: Mirabel and the Gravity
premise: Mara Vane has spent twelve years as a cargo hauler in contested orbits, tending a terraforming garden on the moon Meridian for colonists who won't arrive for another century. When a manifest lists her under a name she buried during the war, she learns she's been flagged as the courier of a dead scientist's final transmission — proof that the ceasefire both factions signed was built on a lie. Hunted by her former comrades and the government that erased her, Mara must choose between delivering the message and protecting the fragile new identity she's built. She delivers it, exposing the truth at the cost of her anonymity, and plants the garden's first seed in open soil as the war reignites around a population finally told why.
about_author: Felix Nystrom is the pen name of a former logistics analyst who spent six years writing orbital traffic reports before turning to fiction. He lives in Tromsø, where the long winters taught him that survival is mostly a matter of what you're willing to carry.

chapters.title: Manifest Anomalies
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. During a routine cargo audit, Mara finds her old name — Ilsa Rehn — listed on a ship decommissioned before the war ended. The emotional beat is quiet dread: someone has reached into her buried past, and the system that hid her is now pointing at her.

chapters.title: The Garden That Waits
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She retreats to Meridian's terraforming dome, checking seed vaults and irrigation lines for colonists a century away. Her caretaker routine shows what she's protecting; the anomaly gnaws at her sense of safety.

chapters.title: A Voice from the Wreck
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Tracing the manifest entry, she finds a cached message from Dr. Edda Solheim, her wartime science officer, recorded before her death: coordinates, a decryption key, and one sentence — 'They knew the colony ship was empty.'

chapters.title: Twelve Years Invisible
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Mara's POV. We learn how Ilsa Rehn became Mara Vane: the evacuation she survived, the records she burned, the guilt of being the only officer who left the Meridian research team behind. Emotional beat: shame wearing the mask of caution.

chapters.title: The Man Who Counts Crates
chapters.summary: Dov Aric's POV. A customs inspector with his own debts notices the same anomaly and flags it upward — not out of malice but ambition. He becomes the story's sympathetic antagonist, believing he's uncovering fraud, not hunting a woman.

chapters.title: First Tail
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Someone follows her through the Kessel Yards; she loses them using hauler tricks, but they scanned her transponder. Rising tension: her invisibility has an expiration date now.

chapters.title: Old Comrades
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She contacts Renn Okafor, her former squadmate turned black-market fixer, hoping he can scrub the record. He warns her the query came from inside the Concord military — her own side wants the name found.

chapters.title: What Edda Knew
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, interleaved with Edda's recovered logs. The logs reveal the ceasefire was negotiated knowing the 'rescued' colony ship carried no survivors — a sacrifice staged to end the war. Loyalty vs. truth crystallizes: exposing it honors the dead or betrays the living.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Dov's POV. Dov is approached by Concord intelligence: help identify the manifest ghost and his debts vanish. He hesitates — the file he's shown feels too curated. Emotional beat: a decent man sensing he's being used.

chapters.title: Seventy-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Renn gets her a window: three days before the flag hardens into a warrant. She must decide whether to run forever or deliver Edda's message to the one journalist still broadcasting outside Concord control.

chapters.title: The Long Haul Out
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She loads her hauler for a delivery run as cover and plots a course through contested orbits toward the broadcast station. Tension builds through near-misses at two checkpoints; she uses her twelve years of unremarkable competence as camouflage.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Dov's POV. Dov intercepts her at a fuel depot, not to arrest her but to ask questions. She tells him enough truth to shake him; he lets her go and falsifies his report — crossing his own line. Their uneasy alliance begins.

chapters.title: Renn's Price
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Renn sells her route to Concord intelligence to buy his family's passage off-world. Mara discovers the betrayal mid-flight. Emotional beat: loyalty isn't betrayed out of evil but out of love, which makes it worse.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Shoals
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Concord fighters corner her in the asteroid shoals. She survives by venting her own cargo and riding the debris wake — destroying the garden supplies she's hauled for years. The price of survival becomes literal.

chapters.title: What the Garden Was For
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, wounded and drifting. She reads the rest of Edda's logs and learns Edda stayed behind voluntarily so someone could carry the truth out. Mara stops running from guilt and starts running toward purpose.

chapters.title: The Broadcast Station
chapters.summary: Mara and Dov's POV alternating. They reach the station, but Concord marines arrived first via Renn's tip. A standoff in the transmitter room; Dov buys her time by claiming jurisdiction over the 'fraud case.'

chapters.title: The Message
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. With marines breaching, she decrypts and transmits Edda's full evidence — including her own war record and real name. Climax begins: she chooses truth over survival, publicly becoming Ilsa Rehn again.

chapters.title: Reckoning
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The broadcast spreads; Concord command fractures, hardliners move to seize Meridian, and the ceasefire collapses into open crisis. Mara is captured — not quietly, but as a known face. Lowest point: the truth may start the war it meant to end.

chapters.title: Trial by Orbit
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Held aboard a Concord cruiser, she faces interrogation from General Ashe, who argues the lie saved millions. Ilsa counters that peace built on stolen grief belongs to no one. The debate is the thematic climax: price of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: The Turn
chapters.summary: Dov's POV. Dov releases his full customs files — including proof Ashe ordered the original cover-up — to the same network. Public opinion turns; soldiers refuse orders to bombard Meridian. Ilsa walks free because the system can no longer afford to hold her.

chapters.title: Open Soil
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. On Meridian, under an uncertain truce, she opens the seed vault and plants the first seeds in raw regolith — no longer waiting for permission or perfect conditions. Emotional beat: grief converted into tending.

chapters.title: The Gravity Between Us
chapters.summary: Ilsa and Dov's POV closing together. The war simmers but holds; the colonists' arrival moved up fifty years. Ilsa keeps her name, her scars, and her garden. Final beat: some truths cost everything and are still worth carrying.
